title: Pediatrics clerkship
audience: a medical student in the clinical years preparing for the USMLE
purpose: Care for children from birth to adolescence: newborn care, growth and development, well-child care and immunizations, nutrition, fever and common infections, respiratory and GI illness, fluids, congenital and genetic conditions, emergencies, adolescent medicine, abuse recognition and reporting, and pediatric dosing.

weeks.5: Fever and common infections in children
weeks.7: Pediatric GI illness and fluid management

blocks.deliverable: Assess developmental milestones at five ages.
Plan a well-child visit with its vaccines.
Evaluate fever in an infant by age group.
Week 7 midterm; estimate dehydration and plan fluids by weight.
Recognize respiratory distress and its causes.
Compute a weight-based dose and check it against a maximum.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Well-child visit simulation: plan visits at 2 months, 12 months and 4 years with milestones, vaccines and anticipatory guidance.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
